ambiguities: Several generic declarations use the token LocalDef008 as a universe-level name, whereas D008 uses it as a real-valued model projection. These are different syntactic roles; the universe occurrences do not refer to the error parameter.

External declarations are supplied only to the stated frontier. In particular, Fin.foldl delegates to an unexpanded private loop. Its standard meaning is an increasing-index left fold; the loop implementation itself is not available for independent inspection here.
The model specifies real-valued operations satisfying error axioms, without specifying a floating-point format, rounding rule, representable subset, or treatment of overflow and underflow.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the computed dot product whose absolute error is bounded.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp, natural numbers t, B, N, equality hN: B^t = N, and functions x,y: Fin N → ℝ, form v(i) = fl_mul(x(cast hN i), y(cast hN i)) for i ∈ Fin(B^t), and return the recursive sum S(fp,B,t,v) defined in D005.
dependency_coverage.name: Computed hierarchical dot product

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target universally quantifies over this type, so all the data and axioms specified by its constructor are implicit model assumptions.
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of arithmetic models. Its supplied constructor D007 packages a nonnegative real error parameter, five real-valued arithmetic operations, exact addition from a zero accumulator, and relative-error axioms.
dependency_coverage.name: Arithmetic model type

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the bound's coefficient at n = t(B−1)+1.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, define γ_n = ((n:ℝ)u)/(1−(n:ℝ)u), where u is the model's error parameter. This is a total real expression in Lean; division by zero has value zero, although the target's hypothesis ensures a positive denominator.
dependency_coverage.name: Accumulated error coefficient

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target assumes this predicate at n = t(B−1)+1, ensuring the coefficient's denominator is positive.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, the admissibility predicate is (n:ℝ)u < 1.
dependency_coverage.name: Error-budget admissibility

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the grouping and summation algorithm used after the individual rounded products.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp and B,t ∈ ℕ, S(fp,B,t,·) maps real vectors of length B^t to ℝ. Its equations are S(fp,B,0,v)=v(0), and S(fp,B,t+1,v)=A(fp,B,j ↦ S(fp,B,t,i ↦ v(j·B^t+i))), where j ∈ Fin B, i ∈ Fin(B^t), and A is D012. Thus it recursively sums B contiguous blocks of length B^t and sequentially adds their results. The definition permits B=0 and t=0.
dependency_coverage.name: Recursive B-ary block summation

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the one rounded multiplication for each input pair.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp, selects its fifth field, fl_mul: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ. D007 requires that for all real a,b there exists δ with |δ|≤u and fl_mul(a,b)=ab(1+δ).
dependency_coverage.name: Model multiplication projection

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Specifies all assumptions carried by fp. Addition, multiplication, nonnegativity of u, and exact zero-start addition govern the target algorithm; subtraction, division, and square root are additional model requirements even though the algorithm does not call them.
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a model from u∈ℝ with 0≤u; operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div: ℝ×ℝ→ℝ and fl_sqrt: ℝ→ℝ; the axiom ∀a∈ℝ, fl_add(0,a)=a; and the following axioms. For every a,b∈ℝ, each of fl_add(a,b), fl_sub(a,b), and fl_mul(a,b) equals, respectively, (a+b)(1+δ), (a−b)(1+δ), and ab(1+δ), for an existential real δ satisfying |δ|≤u. For every a,b∈ℝ with b≠0, fl_div(a,b)=(a/b)(1+δ) for such a δ. For every a∈ℝ with a≥0, fl_sqrt(a)=sqrt(a)(1+δ) for such a δ. Each existential δ may depend on the operation and operands; a common δ is not required. The operations are total, but division at zero and square root at negative arguments have no corresponding error axiom.
dependency_coverage.name: Arithmetic model constructor and axioms

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines both the admissibility condition and γ_n.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp, selects its first field u∈ℝ, whose nonnegativity is included in the model.
dependency_coverage.name: Error parameter projection

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Justifies accessing index zero in the depth-zero summation case.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every B∈ℕ, 0<B^0. In particular, B^0=1 even when B=0.
dependency_coverage.name: Base-level index validity

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes each contiguous-block access in the recursive algorithm well-defined.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For all B,t∈ℕ, j∈Fin B, and i∈Fin(B^t), the natural number j.val·B^t+i.val is strictly less than B^(t+1).
dependency_coverage.name: Block index bound

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Implements the dependent split between depth zero and positive depth in D005; it adds no mathematical hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For any B∈ℕ and universe-polymorphic family P(k,v) indexed by k∈ℕ and v:Fin(B^k)→ℝ, given x∈ℕ, v:Fin(B^x)→ℝ, a value h0(w):P(0,w) for every w:Fin(B^0)→ℝ, and a value hs(t,w):P(t+1,w) for every t∈ℕ and w:Fin(B^(t+1))→ℝ, returns P(x,v) by natural-number case analysis. At zero it returns h0(v), and at t+1 it returns hs(t,v). No induction hypothesis is supplied to hs.
dependency_coverage.name: Dependent depth case split

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Specifies the sequential addition of the B child results at every internal node. Exact fl_add(0,a)=a makes the first addition exact, leaving at most B−1 nontrivial addition errors per level.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp, n∈ℕ, and v:Fin n→ℝ, define A(fp,n,v) by a left fold starting at a0=0 and setting a_(k+1)=fl_add(a_k,v(k)) for k=0,…,n−1; return a_n. For n=0 the result is zero.
dependency_coverage.name: Sequential rounded sum

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the rounded addition used in every sequential sum.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every model fp, selects its third field fl_add:ℝ→ℝ→ℝ, subject to the addition error axiom and fl_add(0,a)=a in D007.
dependency_coverage.name: Model addition projection

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses B^t=N, the exact-zero addition law, and all operation model equations.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an arbitrary sort α and a,b∈α, Eq(a,b) is the proposition that a and b are equal.
dependency_coverage.name: Equality

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Represents vector indices and recursive block indices. Since B>0 and N=B^t, the target's input index set is nonempty.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every n∈ℕ, Fin n is the type of natural numbers k with 0≤k<n, represented by a natural value and a proof of its strict upper bound.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Allows the exact sums in the target to range over every input index.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Uses natural-number monoid powers for the lengths B^t; in particular, the zeroth power is one.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Is the domain of t, B, N, the error index, and all index values. Negative depths and sizes are excluded.
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type ℕ of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.name: Natural numbers

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes all non-strict real comparisons ordinary real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real non-strict order

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes x_i y_i, nu, and multiplication by γ_n exact real products, distinct from calls to fl_mul.
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary multiplication operation on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.name: Exact real multiplication

dependency_coverage.meaning: Real subtraction defined by a−b=a+(−b).
dependency_coverage.name: Exact real subtraction

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the maximum operation needed for ordinary real absolute value.
dependency_coverage.meaning: The lattice structure on ℝ inherited from its distributive lattice, with supremum max and infimum min.

binders: For every arithmetic model fp of the type described by D002 and D007, with error parameter u.
For every t,B,N∈ℕ, in that order.
For every proof ht of 0<t, proof hB of 0<B, and equality hN:B^t=N.
For every pair of real vectors x,y:Fin N→ℝ, after the size equality has been supplied.
conclusions: The conclusion is an absolute forward-error bound against the exact real dot product. The scale is the sum of absolute exact products, equivalently the ℓ¹ norm of the componentwise product vector; it is not a bound relative to the absolute exact dot product.
hypotheses: The model contains u∈ℝ with u≥0 and total real-valued operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div, and fl_sqrt.

For each a,b∈ℝ and separately for addition, subtraction, and multiplication, there exists a real δ, possibly depending on the operation and a,b, with |δ|≤u such that the computed operation equals its exact real result multiplied by 1+δ.
For every a,b∈ℝ with b≠0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_div(a,b)=(a/b)(1+δ).
For every a∈ℝ with a≥0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_sqrt(a)=sqrt(a)(1+δ).
The depth and branching factor satisfy t>0 and B>0; the vector length satisfies N=B^t.
For m=t(B−1)+1, the additional hypothesis is (m:ℝ)u<1. Consequently m≥1, N≥1, u<1, and 1−(m:ℝ)u>0.
No sign, nonzero-entry, representability, or normalization condition is imposed on x or y.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n denotes {0,…,n−1}. The cast along hN:B^t=N preserves the underlying index.
Natural subtraction is truncated at zero. In m=t(B−1)+1 it agrees with ordinary subtraction because B>0.
Define A(fp,n,v) by a0=0 and a_(k+1)=fl_add(a_k,v(k)) for k=0,…,n−1, and return a_n.
Define S(fp,B,0,v)=v(0). For d∈ℕ, define S(fp,B,d+1,v)=A(fp,B,j↦S(fp,B,d,i↦v(j·B^d+i))), with j∈Fin B and i∈Fin(B^d).

Define C(fp,t,B,N,hN,x,y)=S(fp,B,t,i↦fl_mul(x(cast hN i),y(cast hN i))). The algorithm rounds each individual product, recursively processes contiguous blocks, and sequentially adds the B child results at each node.
For n∈ℕ, γ_n=((n:ℝ)u)/(1−(n:ℝ)u), and admissibility at n means (n:ℝ)u<1.
All arithmetic in the exact reference sum, the absolute values, and the bound is ordinary real arithmetic. For a∈ℝ, |a|=max(a,−a).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-arithmetic model satisfying the supplied relative-error axioms and exact addition from zero, every positive natural depth t and positive natural branching factor B, every N=B^t, and all real vectors x and y of length N, compute each component product using the model's multiplication and sum those products by the specified recursive B-ary contiguous-block algorithm. If m=t(B−1)+1 satisfies mu<1, then the absolute difference between this computed value and the exact dot product is at most mu/(1−mu) times the sum of the absolute exact component products.

vacuity_risks: For fixed parameters with mu≥1, the final implication has a false admissibility premise and gives no error guarantee. In particular, since m≥1, a model with u≥1 admits no target instance satisfying that premise.
The model assumptions are satisfiable: exact real arithmetic operations with u=0 satisfy them. Thus universal quantification over models is not inherently empty.
The hypotheses exclude t=0, B=0, and N=0. No empty-vector case occurs in the target, even though some supporting definitions accept zero sizes.
B=1 is allowed. Then N=1 and m=1 for every positive t; every internal sum has one child and is exact by fl_add(0,a)=a, leaving only the individual multiplication error.

When u=0, the bound is zero and the conclusion asserts exact equality. When every exact component product is zero, the right-hand side is also zero, so the conclusion again requires exact equality rather than becoming vacuous.
The guarantee concerns an abstract model with globally valid relative-error axioms. Its application to any concrete implementation depends on that implementation satisfying those axioms.
